summary:
# NOTES: "The Odyssey of a Torpedoed Tramp" (Maurice Larrouy, 1918; Gutenberg #76361)

Narrator: Sonnie / "my boy" (the Pamir's young French officer; engaged to Marguerite of La Rochelle). Letters written to "old man"/"old chap"/"dear old thing" (the narrator's friend, a gunner/sub-lieutenant on the French battleship *Auvergne*; earlier had been on a training ship, was at New Orleans with narrator; had a Chilean sailing-ship ambition). Friend's name not given. Friend's letters referenced but not quoted at length. Friend was once a "sometime lieutenant" to narrator in their earlier days.

Single book, four PARTS, letters with place/date headers. Written in letter form, first-person, colloquial slang, mixed French/English.

## Key characters
- **Fourgues** ("Old Man", "the Old Man", "Skipper"): captain of the *Pamir*. Slant eyes, goatee, from Orange (wife and children there); Provençal accent; swears, "Nitchevo!"; plays cards (fortune-telling; missing nine of clubs); plays English billiards; fond of rum, old brandy, Havana cigars; sometimes "loses his hair" (rage). Calls narrator "my boy", "Sonnie", "kid". Says things come true 6–8 months later.
- **Muriac**: engineer, began at 16 as fireman on coasting vessel; made steel collars for broken shaft (8 bolts). Left at H----.
- **Blangy**: officer, had fever, quinine; left at H----; later commands a half-rotten trawler off Africa/Tunis; reunited in Algiers Jan 1916.
- **Villiers**: engineer of the *Mer-Morte* (torpedoed); Arts et Métiers graduate; neckties; mathematical; joined *Pamir* after *Mer-Morte* sinking; stays on as engineer; calculated Jutland cost (~60 million pounds / "a billion" francs + 500 million human loss).
- **Fabrice / "little Fafa"**: former cocktail-maker at Galveston; went forward.
- **Reservists**: tram-driver (Paris boats-type; taught navigation; "Johnny of the Paris boats"); croupier from Deauville; newsvendor; shopman; cabby; hotel lift-boy; cinema man (movie-man, runs dynamo, later mule-friend); three carriers; bill-poster; cattle-dealer (wrong cocks, boiler 3 tubes blew); chef of Hotel Romantic, Monte Carlo (cooks for officers); Seine boat-owner, reservist chief quartermaster at K----.
- **Owner**: Company owner, in Paris/shareholder-minded; refuses wireless ("not much use"), refuses to pay for *Lamartine* damages; chartered at ~£50/day; "feathers his nest"; Fourgues calls him "the owner".
- **Mousseaux**: civil engineer, Munitions Department, Norman, big blond blue-eyed; on NY trip; argues for guns forward and wireless.
- **Flannigan / Flamigan**: American, Irish father, knew Fourgues on coast of Chili ~10–12 years earlier; carries cargoes Norway/Russia/US; Trondhjem, New York; claims Germans prepare submarine warfare.
- **Plantat**: Old Man, commands *Terre-de-Feu*; friend of Fourgues; Dardanelles pessimist.
- **Villiers**, **Marguerite** (narrator's fiancée, La Rochelle, later wife; she visits Blangy's cabin? no—the "little lady" is a different woman).
- **Little lady** (Bayard woman): wife of a naval lieutenant on cruiser *Bayard* (three funnels, two masts, ram); from a village in the Jura; daughter of a ship inspector; pawned gold watch and ring; sailed from Syracuse on cork-and-sulphur sailing ship to Malta; slept in Customs office at Malta; Fourgues calls her "little girl/little woman"; hugged Fourgues; *Bayard* at Bizerta dry-dock (Sidi-Abdallah).
- Admiral (bachelor) at Malta: angered by wives; "war is war and peace is peace."
- German submarine officer (*Mer-Morte* sinking): speaks French; "We are not savages"; prize-money ("ten thousand marks to commander, five thousand to me, a thousand each for crew").
- Greek government / Constantine / Venizelos / Sophie's husband; Sarrail (General, Army of the East).
- Naval Commodore (destroyers); Commander of *Marguerite* (T.B.D.); *Lamartine* (cruiser, rammed); Admiral of the Fleet at Fano (sealed orders); post-captain (coal order); "Tin Hat" Naval officer at H----; Naval Brass Hat at Salonica banquet (praised Fourgues, "Captain Fourgues will not again find a case like that of the *Mer-Morte*").
- Owner's tin-pot officer at Morocco; Army bloke with mules/aeroplanes; mule-merchant at Cette.

## Ships
- ***Pamir*** (French cargo-boat, nearly 20 years old, built at Birkenhead/Liverpool area builder's yard; ~3,000–3,500 tons; 35 crew; no wireless, no guns; two lifeboats; propeller shaft broken mid-Atlantic, 2 steel collars by Muriac, later K---- collar, later Cadiz repairs; lost propeller chunk and 3 nuts; screw replaced at Cardiff branch; dry dock Newcastle April 1915 (retubed boilers, shaft replaced), later Marseilles dock Oct 1916; lookout masthead installed by Fourgues).
- ***Lamartine*** (armoured cruiser; rammed by Pamir at K----/Anti-Paxo; damaged davits and lifeboat).
- ***Karl Kristian*** (Norwegian cargo; took 2,500 bales cotton + 4,000 more to Copenhagen).
- ***Marguerite*** (T.B.D.); ***Revolver*** (destroyer escort, Argostoli convoy); ***Terre-de-Feu*** (Plantat's ship).
- ***Mer-Morte*** (torpedoed, 5,000 tons munitions, skipper killed; crew rescued by Pamir near Malta–Algiers route).
- ***Worthminster*** (English tramp, Marseilles–Salonica, probably lost; had wireless).
- ***Sainte Eulalie*** (disabled steamer towed to Ajaccio).
- ***Suffren***, ***Provence***, ***Ville-de-la-Ciotat***, ***Lusitania***, ***Hampshire***, ***Cressy***, ***Hogue***, ***Aboukir***, ***Bouvet***, ***Ocean***, ***Gambetta***, ***Invincible***, ***Indefatigable***, ***Queen Mary***, ***Black Prince***, ***Warrior***, ***Defence*** (named losses in discussion).
- ***Auvergne*** (friend's battleship, 80 million francs, 1,200 men).
- ***Bayard***, ***Lyon*** (battleship to Malta), ***Saint-Artémise***, ***Jeanne-Marguerite***, ***Creuse***, ***City of Birmingham***, ***Santa Trinita***.
- German ship at Morocco (Woermann line, bananas & peanuts, rotted).

## PART ONE (Aug 1914 – Feb 1915)
1. **Aug 22, 1914, S.S. Pamir, off Morocco** (letter 1): Pamir loading 5,000 bales of cotton at New Orleans (July 25); sailed 2 a.m.; narrator's watch 3 a.m. for Blangy; 95° on bridge, 104° in cabin in Gulf; shaft broke ~1 yard from thrust block after ~3 days; repaired with Muriac's collars, 8 bolts (two days); drifted 50 miles west. Night of Aug 7 entered Irish Channel; no lights; destroyer fired blank then shell 10 yards ahead; "Stop! Or we'll sink you!"; told "War's declared!"; Fourgues hugged narrator; "Go back to France!"; "Hard a-starboard and full speed for H----". Champagne spilled. Pamir reached H---- at 9 a.m.; Naval officer (Tin Hat) mustered crew; Muriac, Blangy and half deck crew/3/4 engine ratings taken off; reservists sent (5 seamen, 10 engine-room ratings + the listed croupier, etc.). Left H---- 6 p.m. for Morocco port (unnamed "----"). Boiler 3 tubes blew (cattle-dealer let tank empty). Fourgues slowed to 5 knots. Put in at port of ---- on Sunday: coal "mobilization reserve," could not give. Arrived Morocco; wandered with American signalling position. No charts. Ordered to wait; cotton heating; reservists sick. Narrator: "I'm Fed Up."
2. **Oct 5, 1914, Port of K----, Mediterranean** (letter 2): Friend's *Auvergne* praised (launched). Pamir ten days in Morocco rolling; German Woermann hulk untouchable. Coal taken from Expeditionary Corps heap; counted sacks. Orders to Oran, Dakar, then T---- (20 miles north) to transport ~50 Germans driven out of Morocco; Fourgues built wooden deck shelters; piano smashed when cable fouled winch; Fourgues' laugh; owner's Boche with spectacles protested. Cotton bales as mattresses. German old man: "gentleman of rank" lecture; Fourgues: "Get to H---- off the bridge!" Landed Germans at ---- . Owner arrives; Fourgues: "Fifteen hundred bales of cotton gone!" Post-captain orders 3,000 tons coal for Fleet; forward hold 1,500 tons special coal for torpedo-boats; cotton left aft. Narrator left in command at K----.
3. **Nov 15, 1914, Cardiff** (letter 3): Saw friend's fleet off Leuca (3 big ships, line ahead). K---- loading: 1,500 tons lump coal-dust (Grand-Combe Lens briquettes at top, mud below). Anti-Paxo: cruiser (friend's "thirty-six funnel" cruiser) crossed bow; T.B.D. commander ("Marguerite"); to coal cruiser *Lamartine*; rammed Lamartine on "Go ahead! Astern!" — broke two hawsers, starboard lifeboat smashed; davits twisted. Commodore's destroyers coaled (100 tons left). Liverpool: cotton to *Karl Kristian* (Norwegian) — Fourgues: "if he had known... pitched it all overboard" in Morocco. Birkenhead: propeller chunk lost; diver; raft, new screw at Cardiff. Welsh Lino dinner; Fourgues' billiards (100 points in 500; 7 breaks); Fourgues's speech on Austrian blockade (rabbit-hole analogy; mines, 55 fathom line). Narrator "mandolin".
4. **Alexandria, February 12 (1915)** (letter 4): Collar at K---- shook; Cadiz repairs, Muriac's collars back. Franco-British squadron; Senegal, Togoland, Cameroons; Gorée, Sierra Leone, Porto Novo; returned empty; Spain Boche ships; Dakar; Casablanca: 2,000 tons cereals for Montenegro via barcasses; Oran shoes/blankets; Bizerta petrol. Fleet meeting ~10 miles west of Fano (50–60 ships). Fourgues: "Full steam ahead... due North"; sealed orders; Admiral's "But surely you aren't afraid!"; tin-pot Commander: "Asking for a torpedo?" Antivari: bora; Austrian aviators' bombs; corn; hydroplane risk. Crank overheated; convoy-fear; Pamir missing; Fleet searched 24 hrs; ordered to Alexandria. Narrator asks for books.

## PART TWO (Apr 1915 – Sept 1915)
5. **Newcastle, April 8, 1915** (letter 5): Alexandria; Cairo/Pyramids; Port Said: 600 Indian soldiers (condenser breakdown) in Pamir; pigeon-holes (Muriac's/Blangy's cabins). Hindu musicians (flute/drum). Marseilles; Havre; three died; buried at sea. Sunderland: 3,000 tons coal for English Grand Fleet; Fourgues's coal "sub-soil national reserve". English officers questioned; English navy vs French (age/white-haired commanders). Fourgues: left narrator in command ("Put it through!") in ten days; Charing Cross Hotel, London; repairs at Newcastle; narrator "Ready!" in 11 days.
6. **Malta, June 17, 1915** (letter 6): Fourgues Paris trip; owner refused wireless; Admiralty said submarines bluff; lookout masthead installed. Lamartine damages unpaid. Gibraltar, Mudros; field-guns to Gallipoli (Anzacs); Turks shelled; *Terre-de-Feu* (Plantat); Gallipoli evacuation hint; wounded Australians/New Zealanders on Pamir; cots from Morocco planks; rum/brandy/wine given; narrator's shirts as dressings. Malta; narrator's fiancée (La Rochelle; 1,000 francs saved).
7. **Archangel, September 15, 1915** (letter 7): Cabes (Tunis); Sfax; Turcos; Brest rifles for Russia; Trondhjem; Flannigan; convoy of 14; lost cripples; Archangel: stuck docks; Fourgues' Russian officers; "Nitchevo!"; English cruiser to *Youmanie* (England).
8. **Mudros, December 18, 1915** (letter 8): Newcastle, Southampton (motor-cars, tractors to Havre); Marseilles; Estaque; 30 trains cargo; Milo train error; twelve aeroplanes (six taken); Army bloke; Mudros; Dardanelles evacuation.

## PART THREE (Jan 1916 – Feb 1917)
9. **Algiers, January 30, 1916** (letter 9): Blangy met in arcades, trawler; Mer-Morte torpedoed; Villiers joins; Salonica via Admirals; Africans from Salonica; secret route bet: lifeboats found at 6:30 a.m. after going due west (exact point where routes cross); Villiers' story: submarine officer's speech; prize money; *Mer-Morte* blown up.
10. **Salonica, March 13, 1916** (letter 10): 2,000 cubic metres firewood; Naval Brass Hat banquet ("Thank you. I am a sailor"); Cette mules (100 mules; hay; movie-man & croupier); Salonica; Greek exchange 18–20%.
11. **Bilbao, April 27, 1916** (letter 11): Greek students; Bizerta; woman passenger (Bayard); Sidi-Abdallah; Fourgues' submarine navigation arguments (night navigation; hug coast; beaching); Spanish pro-German; ore 3,000 tons.

## PART FOUR (Jul 1916 – Feb 1917)
12. **Baltimore, July 16, 1916** (letter 12): La Rochelle visit; married (wedding Oct 1916, Marseilles); Jutland cost table (sum ~£60 million; 615 million ships sunk; 800 million with repairs; 950 million artillery; coal 20 million francs; human 500 million). Villiers vs Fourgues on submarine vs big ships.
13. **Naples, September 23 [1916]** (letter 13): Steel from New York; Flannigan's 1916 talk; Mousseaux; Brest; Cardiff; mine/submarine strike off Sallys; leaks 40 tons/day; Genoa; Naples.
14. **Marseilles, October 1916** (letters 14–16): wedding; Fourgues' iron lamp; Villiers hookah; Oct 30: narrator's fear letter; Nov 2: forgives; Dec 16 **Argostoli**: torpedoed-fired-upon near Matapan by U-boat; Worthminster sunk (probably); skippers' luncheon; Salonica; Sarrail; Greek king Constantine; "Triumph of the Lie".
15. **Norway, February 18, 1917** (letter 17): Godfather letter (baby class of 1937); Argostoli–Messina–Ajaccio (Sainte Eulalie towed; one man's hand smashed); Lisbon; Bilbao; Brest; mine near English Channel; Liverpool; Bergen; villiers' calc: 150 million tons? (3.5 times round world; 80–100 million tons); Christiansund; German blockade announced.
16. **OFFICIAL STATEMENT (end Feb 1917):** "The German wireless reports the sinking of the Pamir, which is overdue."

## Other notable items
- Narrator's photograph; wife Marguerite; baby expected 1917.
- Narrator's Fourgues' cards: nine of clubs missing.
- Fourgues mentions "Jellicoe's fleet"; Jutland; Kitchener's death; Irish rebellion; Mesopotamia retreat.
- Letters: Pamir cargo details throughout; Authorities: "Forms" and "Form-fillers."
